utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Regarding the first point, in connection with the military expert's report, I think there's no problem. We did ask the Defence to provide its response before the 12th of January. If it does so earlier, all the better. Regarding the question of translation of documents, it has been suggested that the Registry grant an additional 30 hours per month for you to be able to resolve this problem that you are having regarding the translation of documents in your possession. It seems to me that the Registry has already granted you a certain number of hours, but apparently that is not sufficient. We are therefore going to contact the Registry in connection with this matter, and we will see what the Registry will tell us regarding this suggestion that you be granted an additional 30 hours per month. It is true - and I have noted that repeatedly - that within the framework of the cross-examination you have documents in B/C/S, of which we have no translation, either in English or in French. And the Prosecution is also in a difficult position as a result, and everything is becoming complicated as a result. Therefore, it would be important that when you produce a document, that the Prosecution and the Chamber at least should have a translation. And I think we have all seen that that has not been possible. However, on the basis of the practice of the past three weeks, when you produce a document, there's one or two; there's not an avalanche of documents. So I think that the documents that you produce could be usefully translated in advance, and that is why I asked you to inform the Registry that such-and-such a document needs to be translated because it is exhibited. Perhaps the Registry is very busy; yet, within the framework of the cross-examination, if you have documents in support of your cross-examination, it is necessary for us to be able to check the questions you are asking against the documents. Another solution which could be a constraint for the Defence would be when you have a document in B/C/S, to communicate it to the Prosecution, and if they don't have a translation of it made, then that would raise a problem, because you would be in a position to disclose your documents before the cross-examination and that affects your strategy. You prefer to keep them and produce them at the last moment; at least, that is my understanding of the practice of the Defence. But clearly those documents need to be translated, because if you produce a document and you ask a question about it, we need to be able to verify the relevance and make sure that the reply of the witness is in conformity with the question put relating to a document. Therefore, we shall inform the Registry about this, and I shall produce appropriate instructions to our legal officer that we send a memo to the Registry noting the difficulties encountered by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for your support and for your efforts to assist us. In connection with the reply of the Prosecution linked to the expert report, I would like to say that in connection with our request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please start again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment ago you instructed us and the Prosecutor to cooperate in connection with our request. We have received the translation of the expert report but not all the documents attached to that report, and that is why I believe that this is a problem that we will resolve with the Prosecution and, as I have said, we will have our response ready even before the 12th of January. As for the question of translation, I just wish to tell you, Mr. President, that both Defence teams have been given 75 hours each for translation purposes but only for the needs of the accused, which means for communication with the accused. We have not been granted a single hour for the translation of documents. So to clarify this situation with the Registry, we would kindly ask that we be allowed if we don't use those 75 hours for communication with the accused, that we be given a maximum of another 30 hours per Defence team, which we would use for the translation of documents, as I have proposed. So we haven't been granted a single hour for the translation of documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understand you well, you are suggesting to the Chamber to discuss with the Registry once again the question of 75 hours and whether some of those hours could be switched over; is that right? Because there are two possibilities: Either you will contact the Registry, or I will send a memo to the Registry to draw attention to the problem. Perhaps it might be more practical for you to do that first, that is, to contact the Registry in that connection. And depending on the reply of the Registry, you will inform us again, and then I will move on to the next stage. But I think you understand that the Chamber has no control over the budget. I have no personal budget from which I can grant you anything for this purpose. On the other hand, the Chamber has to make sure that the rights of the accused are respected and that the Defence can properly do its work. And this is indeed a problem that you are facing and which the Chamber is aware of. Therefore, I invite you very shortly to inform the Registry about this, to ask them to respond within a short period of time. And if there is no response from the Registry, you will let me know officially, and I think a motion would be preferable. If we agree ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will do as you have advised us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is ten to 12.00. We are going to have the usual break early, and we will continue without a break after that. So we will resume the hearing at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you have requested protective measures. Can you orally explain the reasons for which you requested those protective measures. We are now in closed session? Are we in private session, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to confirm whether you are receiving the interpretation. If you do, just say yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Since you have requested protective measures, we have decided that you will be questioned under a pseudonym, which will be AH. Your face will be protected by a technical system; that means that it will be distorted. Since the blinds have been pulled down, the public in the gallery could not see you. So we have given you a pseudonym. So I am not going to ask you your name, your date and place of birth. I'm just going to ask you to read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to show you. So can you please read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter] .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. We have exactly one hour. Madam Witness, you are first going to be asked questions by the Prosecution. Today this may last for an hour. And tomorrow you are going to be cross-examined by the Defence. So you will be obliged to stay here until tomorrow. Tomorrow we shall resume at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not absolutely sure, however, based on the piece that I have before this Tribunal, I believe that it was the practice for a witness to write her name on a piece of paper that will then be shown to us so all of us are convinced that she is the witness that has entered the courtroom. After that, this piece of paper is destroyed. So if you believe that this is an appropriate procedure, I would kindly ask for you to order for this to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, we intend to adopt a similar procedure which will achieve the same objective. Perhaps the Court could be shown the sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, we have shown you this piece of paper for identification. If this is your name, then just say yes. We are going to show this piece of paper to the Defence because the Defence is right, they need to know that there is no mistake in identity. And they need to know whether this is indeed you. And this is the means of identification. This is the identification, but don't use your name, because your personal data are confidential. This is going to be under seal, because this is the only identification that we have of you. Madam Witness, please look at this paper and verify for us that this is indeed you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the witness at first wanted to add something to this piece of paper. If that is correct, I believe that she should actually write her full name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, we respect the rights of the Defence. Usher, can you please bring me this document for my verification. What we can do now is for the witness to add in her own hand either the first name or the family name for us to have a written document. Madam, on the paper that we have prepared for you, can you add what you want in your own handwriting, either your name or your family name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show this paper to the Prosecution. Can you please show it to the Defence as well. To the accused. Madam Registrar, can you please give me a number under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number P30 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then, P30 under seal. Madam Registrar, can you please show this document to the Judges, who have still not seen it in its integral version. I confirm that the witness has authenticated this document and added either her own maiden family name or her married family name. After we have done these formalities, we're going to proceed and we are going to give the floor to the Prosecution for their questions. Prosecution, make sure you don't mention the witness's name, because the witness is protected. Try to avoid putting questions that might identify her for the general public. I know it may prove to be a different exercise; however, we are aware of your talents, and we believe that you are going to be able to do that without any difficulties whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think you're too kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Madam, could you tell us, without telling us your precise occupation, in what field of endeavour that you work in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of December, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
